missionPremise: The operator walked the deployed Dashboards surface and found the new shell missing functions the live staff dashboard has. The mission is FUNCTION parity, not layout and not look: a staff member must not lose a capability by moving to this product, and how each function renders is a design decision inside the existing visual law rather than a copy of the old chrome. Source: _inbox/2026-08-19_template_city_lens_build_sheet.md, the 'Shell function parity' table, operator-approved 2026-08-19; shell evidence _inbox/2026-08-17_bastrop_dashboard_layout_inventory.md section 'Shell'. The build sheet sequences the shell functions and the fixture-pack extension as the two things that gate everything else, and runs them in parallel.
completionPredicate: A stranger can verify this without me: (1) each of the eight functions is present on the served top bar or named here as deferred with its reason, with no silent omissions - src/shell-parity.test.mjs carries the eight as a walked table so a missing row fails; (2) the CI check-run conclusion STRING is 'success'; (3) the extended first-paint arm was watched FAILING on a late-theme build with raw output, then passing; (4) the class vocabulary count is stated with its counting rule; (5) the addressability gate and the bake-freshness assertion are green, with what was attached to keep them so named; (6) a PR is open, unmerged, undeployed, with its number and head SHA.
scopeBasis: The boundaries follow the dispatch's own division of the repo - web/ is this lane, and src/fixtures.mjs, src/adapters.mjs, src/city-pack.mjs and src/compose.mjs belong to the sibling lane in P:/tmp/t1pack-dash - plus the build sheet's sequencing. Functions were BUILT where the mechanism already existed and honestly DEFERRED where building would have meant inventing a backend, because the visual law's honest-absence rule makes a stated absence a valid deliverable and a fabricated presence a defect. src/server.mjs was edited because the dispatch permits it and because a capability state read from the server is the only way a disabled-with-a-reason claim can be true rather than hand-written. The Connections register was deliberately NOT edited - see openItems - because its disposition column is sequenced to the end of the fan and its vocabulary is a ruling-shaped decision.

The resolver keeps an IDENTIFIED CALLER distinct from a SIGNED-IN PERSON, because per G-11 a product key names a tenant and never a staff member, so staffUser is false on every deployment with its basis stated.
theEight.deferralReason: This deployment configures no identity provider (SHELL_IDENTITY_PROVIDER unset) and the staff auth build is a separate plan row; People and access is itself gated on it. Building a login would have meant inventing an identity system.
theEight.anonymousPath: Anonymous is the default and only path and it works. Nothing this lane added stores per-visitor state on the server - the one POST forwards and keeps nothing - and the single piece of client state is the device-scoped theme preference, which survives a future sign-in untouched. So there is no anonymous work for an auth flip to strand. Asserted as two measured properties rather than as a conclusion in src/shell-parity.test.mjs 'strands nothing an anonymous visitor did'.

theEight.what: A tray with an honest empty state and NO COUNT anywhere - no badge, no number, no dot. The server sends no count field at any depth and the bell carries no text node. The tray's emptiness is a positive determination derived from the pack's own grants through the existing packSources(), and it travels with its counting rule.
theEight.rule: The surface may count a list it is holding; it may never render a number the server asserted. Both halves are asserted - the server side in src/shell-state.test.mjs 'sends no count of any kind, at any depth', the surface side in src/shell-parity.test.mjs 'shows no notification count, and counts only what it holds'.

A test asserts there is no accent field AND no path by which one could arrive: the chrome sets no CSS custom property at runtime, which is the form a fork would take while leaving every file comparison clean.

theEight.what: A Support entry whose enabled state and basis are derived. Disabled today because SHELL_SUPPORT_URL is unset, so no support channel is reachable from here. No invented help content and no fabricated contact.

POST /api/feedback exists and answers truthfully rather than politely: `accepted` means DELIVERED and nothing else sets it true. With no destination configured it is a 503 naming the missing variable. With one configured it forwards with a bounded timeout and reports the destination's real answer. The composer renders the server's basis verbatim and clears the box only on a confirmed delivery, so a report never vanishes into a failed send.

findingsFromDoingTheWork.finding: The capability resolver's first draft echoed every configured value into its basis, including FEEDBACK_DESTINATION.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.why: A feedback destination is typically a signed webhook whose URL carries the secret, and GET /api/shell is served to an anonymous browser. The support URL is different - it IS the link a person clicks - so the asymmetry is deliberate rather than blanket redaction.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.disposition: FIXED in this PR. Only the support URL travels. A test asserts BOTH directions, because 'nothing is echoed' would be satisfied by a resolver that had also stopped giving the support link.

findingsFromDoingTheWork.finding: A locally-computed 12px type floor went red on the type law's ONE NAMED EXCEPTION, the evidence chip label at 10px.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.why: src/type-conformance.test.mjs already owns the floor and carries that exception by name, added at G-76 after a card falsified the gate's original absolute form. A second, weaker copy of the rule would have been the CTRL-1 shape - one rule, two implementations, the newer one ignorant of the older one's exception set.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.disposition: FIXED in this PR. The local check was replaced with a COVERAGE check that the existing gate still pins 12, still carries the named exception, and still reads the file the new chrome lives in.

findingsFromDoingTheWork.finding: The city-name gate fired on src/theme.mjs, which had joined the scanned markup population the moment it became a served script.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.why: A draft comment cited the predecessor by city name. The gate is case-insensitive across every markup source derived from server.mjs, and it worked.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.disposition: FIXED in this PR. The predecessor is cited as 'the live staff dashboard', and the file now carries a note saying why.

findingsFromDoingTheWork.finding: Two test predicates were written as substring scans and produced false positives on the first run.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.why: A 'no count' key walk fired on capabilities.account, which contains 'count'. An identity-consumption scan read `identity.stateBasis` out of a PROSE COMMENT explaining why it is NOT rendered, and read `identity.environment` out of `identity.environmentBadge`.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.disposition: FIXED in this PR. The count rule splits keys into camelCase WORDS; the consumption rule strips comments and requires a word boundary. Both corrections are documented at the assertion, because measuring the class you report and not reading prose as behaviour are the same two rules this repo has already paid for one layer up.

findingsFromDoingTheWork.finding: req.destroy() on an oversized POST body tears down the socket the honest 400 still has to be written to.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.why: The client would have seen a connection reset, which is indistinguishable from the server falling over - a silent failure in place of a stated reason.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.disposition: FIXED in this PR. The body is drained and discarded so the answer stays deliverable, with a test that posts 64KB and asserts a 400 with its basis.

findingsFromDoingTheWork.finding: The head script's localStorage read is a new way for the G-89 fix to fail.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.why: getItem THROWS, rather than returning null, in a partitioned or blocked storage context. An unguarded throw would abort the whole script before data-surface was stamped - reintroducing the exact flash G-89 closed, through the door this change opens.
findingsFromDoingTheWork.disposition: GUARDED and TESTED. The read is inside try/catch, it runs AFTER the surface stamps, and 'storage throws' is one of the five accepted first-paint cases rather than an afterthought.

openItems.item: Two Connections register rows are now partly false and this lane deliberately did not edit them.
rows: src/shell-homes.mjs SHELL_HOMES, 'other' table: { job: 'Auth / session / notifications / theme / sign out', home: 'Top bar; People and access', disposition: 'Not built' }

openItems.why: Both rows BUNDLE built and unbuilt legs - theme, notifications and the account chrome are built; session and sign-out are not - and the disposition vocabulary is CLOSED at six values (Mounted, Empty, Not built, Island, Killed, Not connected), so no single value is true for either row. The counting rule is pinned to a doc_repo markdown this lane cannot commit, and the build sheet sequences the Connections re-bake to the END of the fan because its disposition column is a function of everything above it. DEV_PROCESS 5.4: propose, do not unilaterally remediate.
openItems.recommendation: Either split the auth row into its four jobs and re-derive the counting rule, or move the nuance into the home text - which is what the file's own comment says the home column is for - and set the disposition from the unbuilt leg. Splitting is the better shape and it is a ruling, not an edit.

openItems.item: The three environment variables this card introduced are unset on every deployment, and each one is the whole difference between a control that explains itself and a control that works.
openItems.note: SHELL_SUPPORT_URL and FEEDBACK_DESTINATION are each one value away from a working capability and need no further build. SHELL_IDENTITY_PROVIDER is not: it gates a sentence, not a login, and the staff auth build is its own plan row. Setting it without that build would enable a Sign in entry that leads nowhere, which is the failure this whole card was written against. FEEDBACK_DESTINATION must be treated as a secret - the resolver deliberately never echoes it.

openItems.item: A per-pack accent is unbuilt and is a product-line decision.
openItems.note: It needs a token-override mechanism that does not fork web/sc-kit.css, plus a pack schema field in src/city-pack.mjs, which is another lane's file. The chrome currently sets no CSS custom property at runtime and a test forbids it, so the decision cannot be made accidentally.

openItems.item: Record search remains an open operator question from the build sheet: build a register, or keep it honestly Not built.
openItems.note: It is kept honestly stubbed by this lane and is now wired to the derived capability, so answering the question later is a backend change rather than a markup change.

openItems.item: The theme is proven by a modelled cascade, not by a browser.
openItems.note: Deliberate and stated: CI is npm ci plus npm test on a bare Node image, and a test that silently skips when Chrome is absent is a control that never fires - the same reasoning G-89 recorded. The compensating discipline is that the model throws by name on any syntax it has not been taught, and both refusals are themselves tested. A rendered check belongs with whoever next runs a real browser against the deployed surface.
